dedupe_keys.name: national highways strategic road network model and hapms network layer england

description: National Highways publishes two geometric descriptions of the strategic road network in England. The Network Model contains links and nodes of the network with their locations, road names, number of lanes and carriageway widths; it is derived from Ordnance Survey Highways data and validated against the RedLine boundary of the network, and it is shared as a file geodatabase through ArcGIS Online. The HAPMS network layer gives the network in the schema of the Highways Agency Pavement Management System, as a zipped shapefile with a PDF guide on data.gov.uk, last modified in September 2026; the Pavement Asset Management System (P-AMS) replaced HAPMS in spring 2023. Coverage is national for the motorways and major A roads that National Highways runs. Both are free under the Open Government Licence version 3. Caveats: only the strategic road network is covered, not local roads, and the two layers use different schemas. The data support network models of the English trunk roads, exposure of links to floods and other hazards, and capacity and resilience studies. They complement the WebTRIS traffic counts and the DfT road traffic counts catalogued here.
